items.title: What One Bad Night Of Sleep Did To My Blood Sugar
items.summary: Sleep and metabolic health are more connected than most people realize, and this was a chance to see it play out in real data while traveling. After a night with only 6 hours and 24 minutes of sleep, average glucose rose 10 points and waking glucose increased 3 points compared to a night with over 8 hours. Just one night of poor sleep can raise hunger hormones like ghrelin and elevate blood sugar, which is why consistent, high-quality sleep is one of the more overlooked levers for metabolic health, especially for women. #GlucoseMonitoring #SleepHealth #MetabolicHealth #FemaleLongevity #ContinuousGlucoseMonitor #WomensHealth #SleepScience

We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. Dr. Tania Dempsey, MD, trained in internal medicine at Johns Hopkins before leaving conventional practice to focus on mast cell activation syndrome, a condition she believes explains far more chronic illness in women than most doctors realize. She's the founder of The AIM Center for Personalized Medicine and helped found the International Society for Mast Cell Activation Syndromes, where she now serves as treasurer. Dr. Dempsey estimates it may affect as many as one in five people, and in women it hides behind a long list of other labels, PMOS, endometriosis, hypermobility, unexplained heavy periods, that rarely get connected back to the same root. items.title: What Birth Control Actually Does To Your Bone Density
items.summary: Birth control is one of the most common questions in women's health, and the decision is never one-size-fits-all. Hormonal birth control suppresses natural estrogen and progesterone production, which over time can affect bone density, something rarely explained at the point of prescription. This isn't about telling anyone to stop taking it. It's about making the decision an informed one, including lower-hormone options and how to support bone health if staying on it. #WomensHealth #FemaleLongevity #BirthControl #HormoneHealth #BoneHealth #WomensWellness #LongevityTips
